proof: The left threshold is $1/m-br/a<0$, since $b>\kappa(a+b)$ and $\kappa\ge1/2$ imply $db>a$. The right threshold is $1/m+r=1$. Thus in each direction the left endpoint is fully captured with empty closed residual, and the right capture is a tangent vertex. The normalized endpoint residual roots are $0,b$, while the reference midpoint root is $\kappa(a+b)/2$. The overshoot is consequently the stated positive number in each of the $m$ directions. The sum of the coefficients is $-mbr=-db$. Decreasing every coefficient strictly lowers all left thresholds and raises all right thresholds, preserving the residual volumes while making all right captures empty. The convex hull and its exact midpoint section are unchanged and all middle traces remain canonical.
statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $m=d+1$, $r=d/m$, $\kappa=(1-r^d)^{1/d}$, $\psi(q)=\min\{1,\max\{0,1-q\}\}$ and $\phi(q)=(1-\psi(q)^d)^{1/d}$.

Let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex of centroid zero and volume $V>0$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i=1/m+\ell_i$ for $1\le i\le m$. The convex hull of the lifts of $A=aT+\delta$ at $-1$ and $D=bT-\delta$ at $1$, with $a,b>0$, has actual midpoint fiber $K=((a+b)/2)T$. Take ambient halfspaces $H_i=\{(z,x):\ell_i(x)+\beta_i z\ge0\}$, with $B=\sum_i\beta_i$. Their endpoint barycentric cutoffs on the reference $T$ are
$$
q_i^A=1/m-\ell_i(\delta)/a+\beta_i/a,\qquad
q_i^D=1/m+\ell_i(\delta)/b-\beta_i/b.
$$
They satisfy
$$
\sum_iq_i^A=1+B/a,\qquad\sum_iq_i^D=1-B/b,\qquad
a q_i^A+b q_i^D=(a+b)/m.
$$
The endpoint capture fractions are $\psi(q)^d$. The actual volume roots of the residuals are $aV^{1/d}\phi(q_i^A)$ and $bV^{1/d}\phi(q_i^D)$. The closed residual is empty for $q<0$ and tangent for $q=0$, while the capture is tangent for $q=1$ and empty for $q>1$. For $0<q<1$ both have positive volume.

Define the normalized residual-root overshoots
$$
\Delta_i=\frac{a\phi(q_i^A)+b\phi(q_i^D)-\kappa(a+b)}2,
\qquad \widehat\Delta_i=V^{1/d}\Delta_i,
$$
where $\widehat\Delta_i$ is the actual overshoot in volume-root units.

If $b>\kappa(a+b)$, the choices $\delta=0$ and $\beta_i=-br$ for all $i$ give $B=-db$. Every left endpoint closed residual is empty, every right endpoint capture is a tangent vertex, and all $m$ canonical overshoots equal $(b-\kappa(a+b))/2>0$. Decreasing the common coefficient makes every right capture empty with the same root losses.
title: One simplex drift makes every canonical residual overshoot positive
